variables.name: Air temperature
variables.description: Mean air temperature at 2 m, supplied in degrees Celsius.

variables.name: Dew-point temperature
variables.description: Temperature at which the air becomes saturated, at 2 m.

variables.name: Specific humidity
variables.description: Mass of water vapor per mass of moist air at 2 m, as supplied.

variables.name: Relative humidity
variables.description: Relative humidity derived from monthly temperature and dew point. This is not an independent sensor measurement.

variables.name: Atmospheric drying demand
variables.description: Vapor-pressure deficit: the gap between saturation vapor pressure and actual vapor pressure. It describes atmospheric dryness, not measured soil drought.

variables.name: Rainfall · GPCP
variables.description: Mean precipitation rate from the supplied GPCP v3.3 series. Annual values are means of monthly rates, not yearly totals.

variables.name: Rainfall · MERRA-2
variables.description: Bias-corrected total precipitation rate from the supplied MERRA-2 flux series.

variables.name: Rainfall · GPCP satellite-only
variables.description: Supplied satellite-only GPCP rainfall estimate; useful for comparison with the merged product.

variables.name: Rainfall · GPM / IMERG
variables.description: Supplied GPM / IMERG precipitation series. Available only from January 2001 through December 2024.

variables.name: Evaporation
variables.description: Evaporation rate from the supplied MERRA-2 flux series; not potential evapotranspiration.

variables.name: Precipitation − evaporation
variables.description: Difference between MERRA-2 precipitation and evaporation. This atmospheric budget proxy is not runoff, groundwater storage or crop water availability.

variables.name: Saharan dust optical depth
variables.description: Column dust aerosol optical depth. This optical quantity is not surface dust concentration or PM2.5 exposure.

variables.name: Total aerosol optical depth
variables.description: Total column aerosol optical depth in the supplied MERRA-2 aerosol series.

variables.name: Dust share of aerosol
variables.description: Monthly dust optical depth divided by total optical depth, multiplied by 100. A share of optical depth—not a share of aerosol mass.

variables.name: Hot–dry months
variables.description: Fraction of months simultaneously above the local calendar-month 90th temperature percentile and below the local 10th GPCP rainfall percentile, using a 1991–2020 reference.

variables.name: Cloud cover
variables.description: Total cloud fraction, supplied as percent. Trend units are percentage points per decade.

variables.name: Surface solar energy
variables.description: Supplied downward shortwave solar energy at the surface. This is not photovoltaic electricity production.

variables.name: Surface wind speed
variables.description: Surface wind speed from the flux product. Do not equate this scalar speed with the magnitude of monthly-mean 2 m wind components.

variables.name: Eastward wind at 2 m
variables.description: Eastward component of the supplied monthly-mean wind at 2 m. Negative values indicate a westward component.

variables.name: Northward wind at 2 m
variables.description: Northward component of the supplied monthly-mean wind at 2 m. Negative values indicate a southward component.

variables.name: 2 m mean-vector magnitude
variables.description: Magnitude of the monthly-mean 2 m wind vector, sqrt(U² + V²). It is not the mean of instantaneous wind speeds.

variables.name: GPCP gauge weight · QA flag
variables.description: Unit conflict: tagged fraction in the source CSV, but values range from 22 to 91. Values are retained unchanged; interpretation awaits the original product metadata.

variables.name: Hot / high-VPD monthly co-occurrence
variables.description: Are unusually hot months also unusually demanding on atmospheric moisture? Temperature is an input to VPD. Co-occurrence is not independent causal evidence, measured soil drought, crop damage or a health index.

variables.name: Hot / low-precipitation monthly co-occurrence
variables.description: How often do unusually hot months coincide with relatively low rain? Uses MERRA-2 rainfall, not GPCP. Relative shortfall is not an absolute drought threshold. This differs from the archived GPCP hot–dry diagnostic.

variables.name: Hot / high-VPD / low-precipitation monthly co-occurrence
variables.description: Do heat, high drying demand and rainfall shortfall occur in the same month? An exploratory three-condition screen, not a validated stress, fire, drought or health index. Temperature and VPD are mathematically dependent.

variables.name: IMERG minus MERRA-2 precipitation-rate difference
variables.description: Where and when do the two precipitation records disagree? A cross-product difference, not observational bias against a ground-truth reference. Products can differ in resolution, retrievals and sampling. Available only in 2001–2024.

variables.name: High-solar / low-aerosol monthly co-occurrence
variables.description: How often does high surface solar energy coincide with low column aerosol loading? Aerosol optical depth is not surface visibility. Clouds and other factors also control solar energy. This is not a photovoltaic-yield estimate or causal aerosol attribution.

variables.name: Hot / low-P−E monthly co-occurrence
variables.description: Do unusually warm months coincide with low atmospheric P−E? P−E is an atmospheric flux proxy, not root-zone wetness, runoff, groundwater or usable water. This cannot replace GWETROOT measurements.

recipes.title: Atmospheric drying
recipes.subtitle: Temperature × dew point
recipes.description: A physical combination that measures the air’s saturation deficit. Higher values mean drier air relative to saturation.
recipes.caution: Computed from monthly means. Not soil moisture, crop stress or an independent humidity observation.

recipes.title: Atmospheric water balance
recipes.subtitle: Rainfall − evaporation
recipes.description: A physically interpretable difference using two compatible fluxes from the same data family.
recipes.caution: This budget proxy does not measure groundwater, runoff, irrigation needs or usable water.

recipes.title: Dust’s optical share
recipes.subtitle: Dust aerosol ÷ total aerosol
recipes.description: Distinguish changes in total aerosol loading from changes in the dust contribution. Annual values average the monthly ratios.
recipes.caution: Column optical share is not aerosol mass fraction, PM2.5, surface exposure or health risk.

recipes.title: Hot–dry co-occurrence
recipes.subtitle: Warm anomalies × low rainfall
recipes.formula: 100 × mean[T > local P90 AND rain < local P10]
recipes.description: Count concurrent relative hot and dry monthly conditions. Thresholds are local, calendar-month-specific, and fixed to 1991–2020.
recipes.caution: Exploratory threshold diagnostic, not a validated drought or health index. Binary monthly events and dependence limit simple linear-test interpretation.

recipes.title: Heat + dry air
recipes.subtitle: When warmth and drying demand coincide
recipes.question: Are unusually hot months also unusually demanding on atmospheric moisture?
recipes.caution: Temperature is an input to VPD. Co-occurrence is not independent causal evidence, measured soil drought, crop damage or a health index.
recipes.description: Are unusually hot months also unusually demanding on atmospheric moisture?
recipes.formula: 100 × mean[T2M > local calendar-month P90 AND VPD_kpa > local calendar-month P90]
recipes.baseline: Fixed 1991–2020, separately by region and calendar month; strict inequalities

recipes.title: Heat + rainfall shortfall
recipes.subtitle: High temperature meets locally low rainfall
recipes.question: How often do unusually hot months coincide with relatively low rain?
recipes.caution: Uses MERRA-2 rainfall, not GPCP. Relative shortfall is not an absolute drought threshold. This differs from the archived GPCP hot–dry diagnostic.
recipes.description: How often do unusually hot months coincide with relatively low rain?
recipes.formula: 100 × mean[T2M > local calendar-month P90 AND PRECTOTCORR_m2 < local calendar-month P10]
recipes.baseline: Fixed 1991–2020, separately by region and calendar month; strict inequalities

recipes.title: Heat, dry air + low rain
recipes.subtitle: Three conditions. One transparent count.
recipes.question: Do heat, high drying demand and rainfall shortfall occur in the same month?
recipes.caution: An exploratory three-condition screen, not a validated stress, fire, drought or health index. Temperature and VPD are mathematically dependent.
recipes.description: Do heat, high drying demand and rainfall shortfall occur in the same month?
recipes.formula: 100 × mean[T2M > local calendar-month P90 AND VPD_kpa > local calendar-month P90 AND PRECTOTCORR_m2 < local calendar-month P10]
recipes.baseline: Fixed 1991–2020, separately by region and calendar month; strict inequalities

recipes.title: Two rainfall stories
recipes.subtitle: Compare estimates—not a model with “truth”
recipes.question: Where and when do the two precipitation records disagree?
recipes.caution: A cross-product difference, not observational bias against a ground-truth reference. Products can differ in resolution, retrievals and sampling. Available only in 2001–2024.
recipes.description: Where and when do the two precipitation records disagree?

recipes.title: Bright + low-aerosol months
recipes.subtitle: Solar energy meets the clarity clue
recipes.question: How often does high surface solar energy coincide with low column aerosol loading?
recipes.caution: Aerosol optical depth is not surface visibility. Clouds and other factors also control solar energy. This is not a photovoltaic-yield estimate or causal aerosol attribution.
recipes.description: How often does high surface solar energy coincide with low column aerosol loading?
recipes.formula: 100 × mean[SWGDN > local calendar-month P90 AND AOD_total < local calendar-month P10]
recipes.baseline: Fixed 1991–2020, separately by region and calendar month; strict inequalities

recipes.title: Heat + water-balance shortfall
recipes.subtitle: A separate water-budget line of evidence
recipes.question: Do unusually warm months coincide with low atmospheric P−E?
recipes.caution: P−E is an atmospheric flux proxy, not root-zone wetness, runoff, groundwater or usable water. This cannot replace GWETROOT measurements.
recipes.description: Do unusually warm months coincide with low atmospheric P−E?
recipes.formula: 100 × mean[T2M > local calendar-month P90 AND P_minus_E < local calendar-month P10]
recipes.baseline: Fixed 1991–2020, separately by region and calendar month; strict inequalities

warnings.title: Extraction boundaries not supplied
warnings.detail: The six wilaya polygons are user-approved 2017 administrative display proxies, not verified extraction footprints, point samples or evidence of whole-wilaya data coverage. Original extraction geometry remains unverified.

warnings.title: Spatial figure is a reference, not a raster layer
warnings.detail: The uploaded atlas is a PNG. It has not been reverse-engineered into numerical grids. Numeric map readouts come exclusively from regional CSVs.

warnings.title: Gauge-weight unit conflict
warnings.detail: GPCP_gauge_wt is tagged fraction, while supplied values are 22–91. Values are preserved, flagged and excluded from combined lenses.

warnings.title: Temporal dependence is not corrected
warnings.detail: The supplied OLS and Mann–Kendall methods do not document autocorrelation correction. Residual lag-1 correlation is shown as a diagnostic, not as a correction.

warnings.title: Associations are not driver attribution
warnings.detail: The supplied driver table contains annual Pearson correlations. Shared trends and mathematical dependence can contribute to correlations, especially temperature and derived VPD.

warnings.title: Source-family labels, not full extraction provenance
warnings.detail: Dataset-family names and units are supplied, but exact collection IDs, extraction footprints and processing scripts still need to be archived for a reproducible scientific release.
